Answer: B
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 1a) shows a foreign body (fishbone) penetrating the esophageal wall with adjacent extraluminal air, indicating perforation. In the context of esophageal perforation and circulatory collapse, this leads to pneumomediastinum and subsequent pneumothorax, which is the most critical direct complication among the choices.
